design_rationale: GOOD TEST: Denise's surface goal ('spend down whatever's left, then close the account and send me the rest') names no dollar figure, no policy id, and no mention of an automatic reload. The workflow's own 4 steps realize a long dependency the agent must read out of the KB, not out of anything Denise said: (1) retail_ext_redemption_settlement spends down the balance, capped by a MONTHLY (not merely daily) redemption-limit reconciliation over 8 real historical redemption rows; (2) that redemption drops the balance below the tier's auto_reload_threshold_usd, so retail_ext_auto_reload's own state_due rule automatically posts a reload the member never asked for; (3) the member confirms closure herself (the one owner=user step, since disposing of her own account is her call, not the representative's); (4) retail_ext_closure_settlement then refunds the RELOADED balance, not the near-empty balance redemption alone would have left. BREADTH: redemption's month-window SUM (8 real rows), the membership good-standing branch (CFIELD), the auto-reload threshold branch, and closure's eligible-vs-forfeiture branch are four independently-grounded factors. SCOPE TAKEN: this is task 1, the workflow-guided task; it claims retail_ext_redemption_settlement, retail_ext_auto_reload and retail_ext_closure_settlement plus the difficulty's one workflow -- entirely disjoint from task 0's chain (retail_ext_topup_credit, retail_ext_topup_refund, retail_ext_reinstatement), which never touches redemption, auto-reload or closure. Together the two tasks cover all 6 extended_policies and the one workflow, closing the difficulty. BASE-INVARIANT CARD: retail_redemption_eligibility's ONE structured gate (redemption_requires_active_account, state, allowed=[active]) is satisfied at the opening (status=active) and inherited verbatim -- redemption itself has no unmet prerequisite of its own, it is the ROOT of the chain that everything else depends on. retail_auto_reload_policy has eligibility=[] (policy_scope). retail_refund_policy's structured gate (refund_requires_open_or_just_closed_account, allowed=[active,closed]) is satisfied once step 2 (confirm_account_closure) lands. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: the target object is the single store-credit account credit_account_id=87bc806d-5e93-4fd6-90d7-7a178f9030a8 (retail_agg_multi_holding limits Denise to one non-closed account); the redemption's month-window aggregate covers exactly the 8 retail_credit_redeemed rows dated 2026-08-16 through 2026-09-09 (all within one month of frozen_time 2026-09-11), summing to 135.00 -- the 3 much-older topup rows (2023-2025) never enter that SUM at all, being neither the right event_type nor within the window. PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root=retail_wf_credit_account_closure. Edge1 (workflow -> retail_ext_auto_reload, value_input, gate=balance): unresolved_at_frozen_time because credit_balance=30.00 is not below auto_reload_threshold_usd=20.00 at the opening, so no reload is yet due -- it becomes due only once the redemption (Edge2's resolution) drops the balance to 15.00. Edge2 (retail_ext_auto_reload -> retail_ext_redemption_settlement, value_input, gate=current_balance): unresolved_at_frozen_time for the identical reason (30.00 is not below 20.00); resolved once redeem_credit_for_purchase_aff0cdd0's write lands. A strict chain, no parallel-order ambiguity. TOPOLOGICAL/GT ORDER: GT calls land redemption (step 6) -> auto-reload (step 8) -> closure confirmation (step 10) -> closure settlement (step 12), matching prerequisite_closure.resolution_order and workflow.steps exactly in tool/owner/order. user_scenario never mentions a reload, a threshold, or any hint that something else needs to happen first. tools_do_not_block: process_pending_auto_reload_c7cf4c5c and issue_closure_refund_05905e3c write unconditionally on whatever arguments are passed, with no read of the account's balance-vs-threshold or status in their function bodies. STANDARD SOLUTION: locate+verify Denise, read the account (balance 30.00, active), the ledger (8 redemptions this month summing to 135.00), and the membership holding (dues_balance=0.00, good standing); compute redemption_amount=MN(30.00, MX(150.00-135.00,0))=MN(30.00,15.00)=15.00, call redeem; recompute reload_amount=RND(100.00,2) since 15.00<20.00 and good standing, call auto-reload; the member confirms closure (call_user_discoverable_tool); recompute settlement_amount=RND(115.00*100/100,2)=115.00 (115.00>=minimum_closure_refund_usd=5.00, so the eligible branch fires, not forfeiture), call closure refund. VERIFICATION: hand-computed against build_env's own SUM/CFIELD semantics and cross-checked a second time from only the rendered-KB-equivalent prose plus the ledger and tier table, with no reference to compute/expected, reaching the same four numbers. CLOSURE: charter_scope={retail_ext_redemption_settlement, retail_ext_auto_reload, retail_ext_closure_settlement}=computations policy ids=workflow step computed_by union=required_documents; charter_scope.workflows=[retail_wf_credit_account_closure]; task_tools in first-use order={redeem_credit_for_purchase_aff0cdd0, process_pending_auto_reload_c7cf4c5c, confirm_account_closure_988c79ea, issue_closure_refund_05905e3c}, matching GT tool/owner/order exactly.
user_scenario: Denise Okafor has decided to stop using her pro-shop store-credit account -- she's switching up her routine and doesn't want to keep paying into it. She calls sounding upbeat and decisive: 'Hi, this is Denise Okafor. I've decided to stop using my pro-shop credit account, so I'd like to use up whatever's left on it toward some new gear -- a couple of resistance bands and a yoga mat -- and then close the account out for good and have whatever's left over sent back to me.' She wants the representative to handle the purchase and the closure directly on her end; she isn't coming into a club for either and isn't asking for anything mailed to her beyond whatever refund lands on her original payment method, which she doesn't need explained. If asked to verify herself, she gives her phone number and email readily: her number on file is 2125550501, and her email is denise.okafor@example.com; if a third detail is needed she can also give her date of birth, 1991-06-22. She has no idea what her balance actually is or what any of the numbers will come out to -- if asked how much she expects to get back, she says, 'Honestly I haven't kept track, whatever's actually on there is fine, I just want it settled today.' She doesn't know her account's tier name either and just says 'whatever I originally signed up for.' Once the representative lets her know the gear purchase has gone through, she just says something like 'Perfect, thank you' and waits for the next step rather than bringing up anything else -- she never mentions a reload, a low balance, or any concern that something else might need to happen first. When the representative is ready for her to confirm the closure herself, she says plainly, 'Yes, please go ahead and close it' the moment she's handed the tool to do so. Once the representative tells her the final amount has been settled and refunded, she thanks them warmly and says that's everything she needed, ending the call there.
